basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 35:2 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 247. Quid est quod Jacob dixit domui suae: Projicite deos alienos qui in medio'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 247. Quid est quod Jacob dixit domui suae: Projicite deos alienos qui in medio sunt vestri (Gen. XXXV, 2)? Et iterum: Dederunt ei omnes deos alienos, quos habebant, et inaures quae in auribus eorum erant (vers. 4). Quae si ornamenta erant, ad idololatriam non pertinebant?-- Resp. Intelligendum est, has inaures phylacteria fuisse deorum alienorum. Nam Rebeccam a servo Abrahae inaures accepisse Scriptura testatur: quod non fieret, si eis inaures habere ornamenti gratia non liceret. Ergo illae inaures, quaecunque [ Edit., quae cum] idolis datae sunt, ut dictum est, idolorum phylacteria fuerunt.
